records.words: A caretaker delivering to five flats, with a Sunday vote on my tea money. Rıza left me his notebook. That name rings a small bell: in Voice, Halil had a friend called Rıza in his goals panel. Low confidence, it is a common name. I will just continue.

Recognition guess at about 3s: Hacer in flat 1. In Voice, Hacer was the neighbour of Halil who stood at the door with him. Low-to-moderate confidence; same name, also a neighbour. Oh, Hacer, I hope it is you. Also Riza from the title. I want to see the building.
A lovely little drawn building with a stick figure in my room. Riza notes are in handwriting. Everyone says their order comes first, so before I run for bread I want to see all five orders.
Five bread orders, all before nine, and reading pauses time, good. I do not know if I carry one order or all of them. Tarik is earliest and top floor. Going to the bakery.
Swap the newspapers of Hacer and Sevim? That is a strange little mischief button. I am curious who would notice, but on my first morning I do not want to play tricks. Taking the bread up to Tarik.
May your legs stay strong: that is a sweet thing to say to someone who just climbed four floors. And I can actually talk back, and time pauses while he talks. Anything new?
Gulls at five. A tiny line but it puts him on the top floor near the roof. Once a day for news, fair. Four others still want bread before eight-something, so I should not sit with him yet.
Oh, I must have picked up everyone bread at once; the next order goes straight to Hacer. Good. I want to meet her.

Be careful around the cat, if there is a cat. Ha. She does not sound like the Hacer who sat in silence at the door with Halil; she sounds drier. Recognition still a guess, now weaker. She tipped me five lira.
Her knee says rain. I want to remember that for later, maybe someone needs an umbrella. Moving on to Sevim.
I noticed. She is not sure she can trust me. I want to know what Tell lets me say.

Just after sixty seconds. I am the new caretaker carrying the morning bread through a little drawn building; four of five loaves delivered, all on time so far. Each delivery opens a short conversation and time pauses while people talk. Now Sevim, who is not sure she trusts me, and Tell lets me pass on things I have heard, as I heard it or for certain, or make something up. I did not know I had heard that Hacer asks about private lives. This is the kind of thing I like: small words with consequences. I think Hacer and maybe Riza are names from Voice, but that is a guess.
I do not want to pass on gossip about Hacer to someone who does not trust me yet. Telling her Tarik is kind, for certain, because he blessed my legs. I want to see if kindness travels.
Everybody knows that. Ha, fair, she is sharp. Asking what is new with her instead.
Her news is: Tarik is kind. The exact thing I told her, handed back to me. A bit hollow; I wanted something of hers. Bread to Burak and Derya now.
Thanks my friend, but he also does not trust me. Derya is not due till nine, so I have time. Trying Sit together.
Oh, that is a lovely line. An accountant, maybe, who knows when numbers are finished but not words. I am glad I sat.
Ten minutes of sitting and he is still not sure he can trust me. I did not see anything happen during the sit, just the one line before it. Asking for his news.
His news is his own water notice, which I already read on the board. So news is mostly facts going around. I am starting to think Anything new is a rumour exchange rather than a chat. Off to Derya.
Derya is the only one without in under her name. I wonder what happens to bread at an empty door.
Bread on the door handle, all five done. No orders now, only Skip. Before skipping I want to read the notebook Riza left.

Sixteen things to learn about people, two found: Hacer sees everyone who passes, Tarik would give me his last lemon candy. I love that second one. A collection of small truths about neighbours is exactly my kind of thing. Looking at Residents.
Walking times from here. I have free morning, so I want to go and sit with Tarik, the lemon candy man.
Sitting with Tarik.
The ferry froze in 1974 and they walked to Karakoy on the ice, and nobody believes him. I believe him! I wish I could say that. I wonder if I can Tell someone this later.
Derya came in from a night shift and went straight up; now she shows asleep. Hung bread was right then. Nothing to do now, so I will just let the morning pass rather than Skip, and see what comes.
Burak went out and left me his plants and his key under the mat. Being trusted with a key by someone who is not sure he trusts me is a nice little contradiction. Going.

I like these people: a frozen ferry nobody believes, a cat that may not exist, an accountant who cannot tell when a conversation is finished. The errands are simple, the little lines are the reward. I am not sure yet whether anything I say travels.
I want to sit with Hacer and see if she is anything like the Hacer I remember.
A retired shop assistant handling family business by the entrance. Not the widowed neighbour from Voice as far as I can tell; I will treat the name as a coincidence now. Sitting with her.

Oh! Sevim told Hacer Tarik is kind on the step. That was my sentence, carried down the stairs. Everyone knows it, she said, but she still passed it on. That is exactly the small consequence I love. They are all on the step now; I want to go and listen.
All three on the step, and I can pick whom to talk to. I want to tell Hacer about the frozen ferry, so somebody believes Tarik.
The ferry is not among the things I can tell. Only the water notice and Tarik is kind, again. I will just look at what Make something up offers; I am not sure I will use it.
Hacer believes what I say, which makes lying to her feel mean. I am only peeking at what I could invent about Derya, whom I have not met.

Romantic feelings for Burak, wow, the game will let me start that. No. But she came home from a night shift, so works hard is barely made up. I will try the unusual reply in its kindest form and see whether it travels like Tarik is kind did.
I am thinking about that. Fair; she has never met me saying anything about Derya. I will watch whether she repeats it. There is a new order due at eight tonight.
A parcel for Sevim waiting in my room. Easy errand.
Sevim is actually down on the step, but the only option is her flat. I would rather hand it to her in person; I cannot see how.
I am at flat 2, Sevim is out, and it offers Go to flat 2, zero minutes. The bread got hung on a handle; the parcel did not. I am standing at her door holding it. Trying once more.

You are already here, there is nothing to pick up or deliver just now. But the order card still says Sevim, a parcel, go to flat 2. Do I have the parcel or not? I guess it needs her in person. She is on the step, so I will go to her.
Leave Sevim parcel here, with Hacer who sees everyone at the door. I would rather put it in Sevim own hands; she is right here. Switching to Sevim.

A widowed retired teacher who corrects the notices on the board. I like her already. But there is no way to give her the parcel she is standing next to; the only parcel button was on Hacer. That is strange. I will sit with Sevim instead.
Forty years of children reading aloud, and she still hears them in the evenings. As a library assistant that one lands right in my chest. I reread it.
Requested phone check, not my own choice. I usually play on my phone, so I am curious how this building fits.

On the phone the building still reads nicely and the buttons are big, but the three name labels on the step pile on top of each other and the stick figures. I could not see the Leave Sevim parcel button or the line saying Tarik is a retired ferry captain in that picture, though the driver lists them. Back to the wide screen.

Tarik is a widowed ferry captain, so the frozen ferry was his ferry. Oh. Now I see Leave Sevim parcel here shows under whoever I talk to; it means here on the step, not with Hacer. Sevim is standing right there, so I will leave it.

For Sevim? Leave it, I will see it gets there. Tarik offering to carry a parcel to the woman standing beside him, with his tired legs. It is a bit absurd, but sweet. Nothing on the board now; I will let the day run.
Everyone went into Hacer flat. I am outside it now, just a caretaker on the step. I am waiting, but for what? The next order, I suppose.
Help Hacer carry a folding work table. For the family paperwork, maybe. Going.
Still fond of the people, but the afternoon is mostly waiting for the next small job, and each person only has one new thing to say per day. The rumour on the step was the high point so far.

I helped carry Hacer table, but she had gone up to Tarik with Sevim, so I carried it alone and she will find it done. Help carry without the person is a bit flat. The neighbours are visiting each other all afternoon without me; I like overhearing whose turn it is to water the landing plants.

Hacer came home and the conversation opened on its own because I was still standing in her flat. She said nothing about the table I carried. I hoped she would notice. Everything I can say to her today is used up.

Hacer: Derya works hard. My half-invented sentence, said to Sevim in Hacer voice. And now Derya says Tarik is kind too. I started two little rumours and watched them climb the stairs. That is delightful and a tiny bit unnerving, since I made one of them up. Derya is awake and on the step; I want to meet her at last.
At last, Derya. A night nurse who is not sure she can trust me. I would rather sit with her than ask her anything.

People are honest at four in the morning. That is a lovely line from a night nurse. Five people, five small true things today. I would like to ask her about the work boundaries option, but I suspect it is a different kind of conversation.
Hacer opened herself again with nothing left to say today. I have met all five. I will let the evening pass and see what Tuesday brings.
Leave the courtyard gate open is new. I do not know who it is for. Maybe the cat that may or may not exist. I am curious.

I met Derya and liked her four in the morning line. Then the gate button did nothing I could see, and now the log says I have already heard these stories today. The people are good; the evening is empty.
Bins from the top floor. Of course. They repeated the same stories, the log says, and so am I. I will carry the bins.

The bins were out before the truck, and Hacer has opened herself again with nothing to say until tomorrow. I have met all five, heard my rumour travel, and now the evening is the same lines repeating. I like these people, but I would close it here tonight and come back to see Tuesday.
Selecting the stopping choice locally by position, because its name has an apostrophe my shell will not pass. I will not type or Submit.

I am stopping on Monday evening at the front step, after the bins. My first day: bread for five, a parcel Tarık offered to pass on, and a table carried for Hacer, who never mentioned it. I loved the small true things people said when I sat with them: the frozen ferry, forty years of children reading aloud, people being honest at four in the morning. Best of all, I heard my own words travel the building, even the one I made up about Derya, which was a little unnerving. But by evening everyone had said their one thing, and the log was the same lines over and over. I would not leave it running. I would come back another evening to see Tuesday, whether anyone remembers what I told them, and whether Tarık ever gets believed about the ice. I am stopping is selected locally; I typed nothing and pressed no Submit.
